entry.dc:title: New Standards for strip mining: social, economic and environmental costs now considered.
entry.dc:creator: Gonnefoy L.
entry.dc:description: The policy behind the Surface Mining and Reclamation Act of 1977 was to balance coal production with environmental standards. At present mine operators are phasing in an interim programme of reclamation while the final regulations are prepared. Mine operators have tried to avoid meeting all the requirements of the interim programme but court cases brought by environmental groups have been decided in favour of maintaining strict compliance.-T.O'Riordan

entry.dc:title: PROGRESS REPORT ON THE COAL VALLEY MINING PROJECT.
entry.dc:creator: Thurston D.
entry.dc:description: Luscar Sterco commenced construction of the mine at Coal Valley, Alberta, in August, 1976. It is designed to produce approximately 2. 5 million clean short tons of steam coal annually - 2. 0 million tons per year being committed to Ontario Hydro and 0. 5 million tons per year being committed to Neptune Terminals for sale on the export market. The project involves constructing a heavy-media coal preparation plant, erecting a 42-cubic-yard dragline, constructing a shop/office complex, and developing three surface mining zones and associated facilities.

entry.dc:title: DEVELOPMENT OF THE WABCO 353FT TWIN ENGINE ELEVATING SCRAPER.
entry.dc:creator: Hurst C.
entry.dc:description: The development of the WABCO 353FT Twin Engine Elevating Scraper for surface mining applications is an example of advancements being made in mining equipment technology. The 353FT optimizes the benefits of the various scraper configurations available by combining the ability to work under adverse conditions, due to its all-wheel drive, with large capcity and the self loading feature of an elevating scraper. Two Detroit Diesel 12V-71T, turbocharged engines drive identical Allison planetary powershift transmissions with variable-input-power torque converters and hydraulic retarders. The tractor engine, equipped with N75 injectors, is rated at 525 brake horsepower (391. 6 kW) at 2100 rpm. The scraper engine, with N70 injectors is rated at 500 brake horsepower (373. 0 kW). The 12V-71T is a 12-cylinder, two-stroke engine. The throttles of both engines are simultaneously controlled through the use of a single throttle pedal which operates two air throttle/cylinders. A second throttle pedal, which controls the tractor engine only, can be used when power from the scraper engine is not required, such as in tight turn situations. Traction sensing differentials automatically maintain torque to the wheels with the best traction. The scraper cutter is driven hydraulically, the elevator electrically.

entry.dc:title: ENERGY OUTLOOK: COAL AS A FUEL.
entry.dc:creator: Gambs G.
entry.dc:description: The author states that the United States should produce 1. 0 to 1. 3 billion tons of coal annually by 1985 to prevent the nation from becoming overwhelmingly dependent upon foreign crude oil and refined products. The author cites the following problems which he claims will prevent this goal from being reached: 1. Clean Air Act of 1970, 2. Federal Mine Safety Act of 1969, 3. Federal Leasing Regulations, 4. Transportation Facilities, 5. Technical Manpower, 6. Mine Labor, 7. Equipment Availability. The United States is fortunate in having one of the world's largest reserves of coal. Total measured and indicated reserves of coal in beds over 28 inches thick and under less than 1000 feet of overburden totaled 434 billion tons as of January 1, 1974. Of these reserves, 297 billion tons were considered underground reserves and 137 billion tons capable of being mined by surface mining. But unless a commitment is made to coal by the Government which will remove the restrictions already in place and prevent other restrictions from being placed on the industry, this coal will not be mined, in the author's opinion.

entry.dc:title: STATE PROBLEMS IN IMPLEMENTING THE FEDERAL SURFACE MINING LAW.
entry.dc:creator: Bowling K.
entry.dc:description: The author discusses some of the problems encountered in preparation of an acceptable state plan that will lead to designation of the regulatory authority.

entry.dc:title: ASSESSMENT OF INITIATING SYSTEMS AND THEIR PRACTICAL EFFECT ON BLASTING RESULTS.
entry.dc:creator: Poole G.
entry.dc:description: The merits of various systems for designed initiating columns of explosives in surface mining activities are discussed with special reference to the quarrying and open-cast mining industries, and a comparative analysis of the practical results which can be expected from each system is made. The importance of the safety considerations involved is discussed.

entry.dc:title: COMPUTER-BASED TOOL PROVIDES ENGINEERING AID IN COAL RESERVE EVALUATION AND MINE PLANNING.
entry.dc:creator: Gillette J.
entry.dc:description: The Surface Mining Simulation System (SMSS) is a set of 16 related mathematical models - with associated equipment, investment and operating cost data - which may be selectively used to simulate the mining of a specific coal deposit. The system allows the engineer to use whatever data available for description of a mining deposit, supplies missing data (in the form of regional averages), and produces information on the best equipment selection, the investment required, the operating costs which would be incurred across years of mining operation, and the profit which would be realized.

entry.dc:title: STEEP SLOPE MINING AND THE SURFACE MINING CONTROL AND RECLAMATION ACT OF 1977.
entry.dc:creator: Sawaryinski T.
entry.dc:description: The author comments on the impact of the Surface Mining Control and Reclamation Act of 1977 on steep slope coal mining operations and reclamation.

entry.dc:title: An assessment of overburden stability in the in-situ gasification of texas lignite
entry.dc:creator: Thompson T.W.
entry.prism:publicationName: Journal of Pressure Vessel Technology Transactions of the ASME
entry.dc:description: In-silu gasification can he competitive with shaft mining for the exploitation of coal at depths too deep for surface mining. The lignite deposits in Texas may be well suited to this process because of their high reactivity, comparatively high field permeabilities and closeness to industrial demand centers. Controlled operation of a gasification facility demands a knowledge of the likely behavior of the overburden and other surrounding rocks. Fracture or collapse of the roof rock can lead to excessive gas loss, water influx arul subsidence effects. The overburden in much of Texas is weak and poorly compacted. Karly roof collapse seems inevitable, and substantial upward caving may occur. Subsidence could be significant if high extraction ratios are used. © 1978 by ASME.

entry.dc:title: ENERGY THEORY SERIES 7: OIL SAND.
entry.dc:creator: Vakabayashi T.
entry.dc:description: Oil sand structure is explained and oil sand deposits in Alberta, Canada, are discussed. Characteristics of bitumens from oil sands of Canada and Venezuela are tabulated. Also discussed are recovery methods including surface mining and in-situ recovery and methods of refining.

entry.dc:title: FRONT SHOVEL WORKS NARROW BENCHES ON CONTOUR JOB.
entry.dc:creator: Mason R.
entry.dc:description: Maneuvering equipment efficiently on narrow benches encountered in contour stripping is a big problem. But Pratt Mining Co. , Kingston, WV, is solving it with a newly purchased hydraulic front shovel. The shovel can dig out overburden and parting from essentially one position, thus relieving congested traffic on the narrow benches, and can also operate close to the outslope without spilling material down the slope - a practice prohibited by surface mining regulations. Pratt Mining adopted contour stripping to maximize recovery of the high quality metallurgical coal and to minimize overburden removal. The easy maneuverability of the hydraulic front shovel makes it effective for both stripping overburden and removing coal.

entry.dc:title: MINERAL OCCURRENCES OF THE SOLOMON ISLANDS: REGIONAL GUIDE TO FURTHER EXPLORATION.
entry.dc:creator: Takeda T.
entry.dc:description: Most of the known mineral occurrences are suitable for either open pit or surface mining method, and are located on or not very distant from the coast. Guadalcanal has discoveries of significant hydrothermal mineralization in the uplifted and eroded core of the deep-seated 'Basement Complex'. Similar discoveries have been made on New Georgia Island.

entry.dc:title: SAVE WATER - TURN TO SURFACE MINING OF COAL.
entry.dc:creator: Corbett D.
entry.dc:description: The paper presents technical and legislative arguments for the use of surface mining method of energy production to provide water storage.

entry.dc:title: INDUSTRIAL HYGIENE PROGRAM FOR A SURFACE MINING OPERATION.
entry.dc:creator: Davis S.C.
entry.dc:description: Utah International Inc. has established an industrial hygiene program which is designed to respond to the special concern of the mining industry and to the changing regulatory environment.

entry.dc:title: SCRAPERS TAKE ON DRAGLINE JOBS.
entry.dc:creator: Chironis N.
entry.dc:description: This article describes how scrapers are beginning to compete with draglines for removing overburden in a significant departure for surface mining. Two examples given to illustrate the successful use of scrapers in removing the overburden above the coal seam are Fuel Dynamics' operations at the company's Kansas and Washington mines. High-speed scraping and the synchronization of scraper operations are highlighted.

entry.dc:title: HOW TO SELECT EQUIPMENT FOR OPEN-PIT COPPER MINING.
entry.dc:creator: Wimpfen S.
entry.dc:description: Guidelines based on mine experience are presented for selecting the type, size and combination of open-pit equipment for copper mining that can help obtain the lowest capital and operating costs for a specific deposit. The principles described are generally also applicable in other types of surface mining.

entry.dc:title: COAL MINE SUBSIDENCE NEAR SHERIDAN, WYOMING.
entry.dc:creator: Dunrud C.R.
entry.dc:description: Studies of coal mine subsidence features in a 30-sq mi area 3-12 mi north of Sheridan, Wyo, indicate that the long-range surface effects of mining thick coal beds underground beneath weak overburden less than about 200 ft thick are greater than the effects of well-planned surface mining practices with proper reclamation and revegetation. Coal resource recovery also is higher and more efficient in most surface mining operations. Subsidence depressions, cracks, pits, and troughs above underground mine workings can render the surface unusuable for development because of the hazard to people and structures. Fires may start by spontaneous ignition in abandoned coal mines if air and water under the right conditions reach surface mine highwalls or underground workings through subsidence cracks, pits, or troughs.

entry.dc:title: UPDATE ON SURFACE MINING LEGISLATION.
entry.dc:creator: Cook C.
entry.dc:description: This article is a continuation of the history of the surface mining legislation commencing subsequent to the sustaining of President Ford's veto by the House of Representatives on June 10, 1975.

entry.dc:title: SURFACE MACHINES OF THE 80's - WHAT WILL BE DIFFERENT.
entry.dc:creator: Anon
entry.dc:description: Trends expected to take place during the next decade in the design of surface mining machines are outlined here. Although no dramatic change in surface mining machine design is expected in the 1980's, there are indications that advances will be made toward increasing machine productivity and reducing maintenance costs. Some will come in the form of size. Mining shovels will become larger, to more effectively match the growing size of haul units. Dragline booms are expected to become longer, to more efficiently cast spoil with an eye to the future, and mandatory, reclamation costs.

entry.dc:title: HIGHLIGHTS OF SURFACE MINING IN 1977.
entry.dc:creator: Anon
entry.dc:description: The topics covered are equipment trends and these specific mineral commodities: coal, precious metals, copper, iron ore, phosphates and uranium.

entry.dc:title: WHAT'S IN THE SURFACE MINING RULES.
entry.dc:creator: Lusk B.
entry.dc:description: The author discusses the key features of the Federal regulations controlling surface mining and reclamation operations, which were published by the U. S. Office of Surface Mining Reclamation and Enforcement. Some of the problems that mine operators must deal with in the face of the new legislation are examined, and a listing of the numerous funds available for research and reclamation is given. Performance standards that coal operators must meet are briefly analyzed.

entry.dc:title: NEW MINING IDEAS ABOUND IN 1978.
entry.dc:creator: Chironis N.
entry.dc:description: The United States' coal industry is participating in a record number of projects involving new operating and equipment principles for improving productivity as well as health and safety in coal mining. Presented here are some of the trendsetters that should influence the direction of mining in the next few years. New concepts and advances in both underground and surface mining, as well as some new processes now being developed for coal preparation are highlighted. One of these is the Battelle hydrothermal coal process for leaching of mineral and organic sulfur compounds from coal.

entry.dc:title: KEYSTONE PREDICTS RAPID EXPANSION.
entry.dc:creator: Nielsen G.
entry.dc:description: An industry-wide survey by The Keystone Coal Industry Manual is discussed and accompanied by tables showing new coal mines, as well as their development and expansion through 1987. The survey shows that new coal production capacity from mines that area currently expanding and developing, combined with production from planned mines, will total about 644 million tpy by late 1987. Although the majority of the new mines will be underground, surface mining will account for the larger share of the production.

entry.dc:title: RESERVES AND RESOURCES OF SURFACE-MINABLE COAL IN ILLINOIS.
entry.dc:creator: Treworgy C.
entry.dc:description: Surface mining accounts for nearly 50% of recent coal production in Illinois, In previous publications, the Illinois State Geological Survey reported that over 20 billion tons of coal in Illinois were potentially strippable. A current estimate, which takes into consideration the present economic and environmental factors, shows that Illinois has 6 billion tons of surface-minable coal in the ground. The amounts of strippable reserves are large in western Illinois and especially in southwestern and southern Illinois, which are more attractive for surface mining because land costs are lower, the heating value of the coal is higher, and the tonnage recoverable per acre is greater. The southwestern and southern Illinois deposits are and will continue to be the major sources of surface-mined coal in the state.

entry.dc:title: Effects of acid mine wastes on aquatic ecosystems
entry.dc:creator: Parsons J.
entry.dc:description: The Cedar Creek Basin (39th N parallel 92nd W meridian) was studied for the period June 1952 through August 1954 to observe the effects of both continuous and periodic acid effluent flows on aquatic communities. The acid strip-mine effluent contained ferric and ferrous Fe, Cu, Pb, Zn, Al, Mg, titratable acid, and elevated H ion concentration, and was toxic to many of the aquatic organisms. In the areas of Cedar Creek, subjected to continuous acid flow, planktonic and benthic species had become adapted to the severe conditions and varied in abundance and diversity. No fishes were observed in the continuous acid effluents area. Downstream, where periodic mineral acid conditions changed drastically during an excessive effluent flow, planktonic and benthic communities had high diversity but low density. The populations of fishes were variable in this stream reach. The chemical basis of water quality variability was shown to be time-related, and statistically related to the aquatic communities. Physical, chemical and biological conditions of acid lakes formed by surface mining were reviewed. In addition to apparent physical and chemical differences in lakes, due in part to variable solar absorbance due to suspended oxides of Fe, chemical variability related to organic composition was reviewed. It is quite probable that degradation of such lakes can be reversed. © 1977 D. Reidel Publishing Company.
